title: Federated Free Storage Mesh - provider admission record
description: One row of the provider registry (Spec S16). It records what has been *verified* about a backend - whether its free tier is real for this account, whether a hard stop exists, whether spillover could become billable - and never what the provider's marketing page claims. That distinction is the whole point of the record, so it is encoded structurally: free_status may only reach a VERIFIED_* value when the accompanying evidence class is runtime_account_evidence, and any row that is not verified free is forced to health QUARANTINED with autonomous_write_allowed pinned false. The same technique closes the other three doors: an external provider cannot be admitted for LOCAL_ONLY data, cannot omit encryption for CONFIDENTIAL data, and cannot claim a provider_id in the reserved 'local_' namespace; and a Supabase row cannot declare itself a bulk object backend. The record carries no credential of any kind - no token, no key, no account identifier - and the field set is closed so that one cannot be added later under a new name. Backend identity is the one thing this schema cannot settle alone. primary_backend and replica_backends are enumerated against the provider registry, so a backend nobody registered is an invalid document; but whether a registered row was actually *admitted* - verified free, healthy, writable, permitted for this privacy class, tier and size - is runtime state no JSON Schema can read. AI_SKILL_LIBRARY/v4/storage/mesh_validator.py resolves that half. Passing this schema is therefore necessary and not sufficient: a placement is admissible only when both halves agree.

adapter_type.description: The integration shape, not a vendor product name. Determines which structural rules below apply.

external.description: True when the bytes leave owned/local storage. Drives the privacy rules below; it is not a free-form descriptor.

free_status.description: UNVERIFIED is the honest default and the state every provider starts in. DOCUMENTED_ONLY records that a free tier is *claimed* somewhere - it is explicitly not a verification and grants nothing. Only runtime/account evidence can produce a VERIFIED_* value.

free_expiry_at.description: Null means unknown, and unknown means NO_AUTONOMOUS_WRITE per Spec S11 - not 'probably fine'.

hard_stop_verified.description: Whether this account has been observed to stop rather than bill when the free allowance ends. False blocks autonomous writes below.

paid_spillover_possible.description: Tri-state on purpose. 'unknown' is not false: Spec S11 makes unverified billable spillover NO_AUTONOMOUS_WRITE, and a boolean would have forced a guess.

health.description: The runtime states of Spec S10. There is no 'UNKNOWN': a provider nobody has probed is QUARANTINED, which is the same fact stated so that it fails closed.

preferred_tiers.description: Spec S17 placement preferences. A preference, never a binding or an entitlement.

acceptable_use_class.description: Spec S17: Hugging Face is for legitimate models, datasets and benchmark corpora, not a generic log dump. The spec names a closed set of provider roles, so this is an enum drawn from policy.yaml provider_roles.acceptable_use_classes rather than a free classifier - a role nobody has agreed to is not a role, and as a 64-character token this field was also key-shaped.

authority.description: A registry row is evidence about a provider, never authority over one. This and authority_flags were defined here and required only in the manifest schema, so every row shipped in providers.yaml carried no authority_flags at all and the guard test passed because it inspected $defs rather than reachability. Required now, on both records.

allOf.title: Verified free status requires runtime/account evidence
allOf.description: Spec S16/S20. A provider's own documentation is not evidence about this account: free tiers change, differ by region, and do not survive an expired promotion. So a VERIFIED_* value is only reachable when the evidence class is runtime_account_evidence and it carries a timestamp and a reference.

allOf.title: Anything not verified free is quarantined and cannot be written to
allOf.description: The fail-closed half of the rule above. UNVERIFIED, DOCUMENTED_ONLY, PAID_ONLY and FREE_EXPIRED all land in the same place, which is the point: 'we read that it is free' and 'we have not looked' are the same amount of evidence.

allOf.title: No hard stop, no autonomous writes
Possible or unknown paid spillover, no autonomous writes
Unknown free expiry, no autonomous writes unless recurring-free is verified
allOf.description: Spec S11 FREE_EXPIRY_UNKNOWN=NO_AUTONOMOUS_WRITE unless the provider is known recurring-free.

allOf.title: LOCAL_ONLY is not admissible on an external provider
allOf.description: Spec S4. Not 'discouraged' - the enum an external row is validated against does not contain the value.

allOf.title: An external provider admitted for CONFIDENTIAL must require encryption
allOf.description: Spec S4/S21: CONFIDENTIAL leaves owned storage only as ciphertext, so admitting the class and not requiring the encryption is a contradiction the registry refuses to hold.

allOf.title: The 'local_' provider_id namespace is reserved for owned storage
allOf.description: This is what makes the LOCAL_ONLY rule in storage_object_manifest.schema.json airtight. That schema permits only 'local_*' backend ids for LOCAL_ONLY objects; if an external provider could be registered as 'local_r2', the guarantee would be a naming convention rather than a control.

provider_id.description: The reserved-namespace rule was carried by a negative lookahead, '^(?!local_)...'. Lookahead is not in RE2, so a Go or any other RE2-backed validator would reject the pattern outright or, worse, silently fail to apply it - and this rule is what makes the LOCAL_ONLY guarantee in the manifest schema a control rather than a naming convention. A load-bearing rule should not depend on a regex feature the next validator may not have, so the reservation is expressed as a separate 'not' pattern that every engine supports.

allOf.title: An owned local store is not an external free tier
allOf.description: Local storage has no free-tier entitlement to verify and no provider that could bill for it, so the cost machinery reads NOT_APPLICABLE rather than being answered with a guess.

allOf.title: Supabase is metadata and index only
allOf.description: Spec S6/S18/S25. Supabase holds the object manifest, not the objects, and it is not authority. Encoded here rather than left to placement logic, because a metadata service that can be declared a bulk backend will eventually be used as one.

allOf.title: Unknowable capacity is not a licence to write
allOf.description: Spec S10/S11. quota_total null means nobody has observed how much free allowance this account actually has, and the mesh cannot honour SOFT_LIMIT, HARD_LIMIT or EMERGENCY_RESERVE against a number it does not have. Until now a row could be external, VERIFIED_RECURRING_FREE, hard-stop-verified and fully writable with quota_total and quota_used both null - a writer with no way to know when to stop, which is the shape a free tier turns into a bill through. Unknown capacity fails closed the same way unknown cost does.

allOf.title: A quota that has not been read is not a quota either
allOf.description: The companion to the rule above: knowing the ceiling without knowing the current consumption leaves headroom just as unknowable.

allOf.title: Only a writable health state may take writes
allOf.description: Spec S10/S19. Previously only QUARANTINED was coupled to autonomous_write_allowed, so OFFLINE, READ_ONLY and NEAR_FULL rows could still be declared autonomous writers - the three states whose entire meaning is 'do not write here'. NEAR_FULL is on this list deliberately: it is the state at or past the 0.92 hard limit, and Spec S10 says no provider should be driven to 100% while another eligible target exists. FREE, HEALTHY and PRESSURED remain writable.

allOf.title: An autonomous writer is a writer
allOf.description: write_enabled and autonomous_write_allowed were independent booleans, so a row could permit autonomous writes to a backend whose writes are switched off, or leave writes switched on beside an autonomous_write denial. autonomous_write_allowed is now the strictly narrower permission it reads as: it implies write_enabled, and every rule above that denies one denies the other. write_enabled without autonomous_write_allowed remains representable, and means exactly what it says - writes are possible, but not without a decision made elsewhere.

allOf.title: An unverified external provider cannot be write-enabled either
allOf.description: The quarantine rule pinned autonomous_write_allowed false but left write_enabled free, which let a row that has been verified for nothing still advertise a working write path.

allOf.title: A health claim needs a probe behind it
allOf.description: Spec S10 lists last_probe_at as runtime state, and the enum comment already says a provider nobody has probed is QUARANTINED. That discipline was applied to the external rows by hand and to nothing by construction, so local_owned_store could claim HEALTHY with last_probe_at null. Any health state other than QUARANTINED now requires a probe timestamp - local storage included, because 'it is our own disk' is a reason to expect the probe to succeed, not a reason to skip it.

allOf.title: The metadata service is pinned to its identity, not to a label
allOf.description: Spec S6/S18/S25. Supabase confinement keyed only on adapter_type, which made the label opt-in: a row with provider_id 'supabase' and adapter_type 's3_compatible' walked straight past it and could declare bulk_object_backend_allowed true. The identity now pins the adapter, so declining the label is itself the invalid document, and the confinement rule below can no longer be stepped around.

allOf.title: An owned local store has no quota anyone has verified
allOf.description: A mutant that survived review: quota_total could be given an invented figure on the local row because the registry test that forbids invented quota numbers skipped non-external rows. Owned storage has no provider-granted allowance to read, so the honest value is null, and it is now structural rather than a convention the next author inherits.

provider_id.description: A stable registry key. Lower-case and underscore-only, so it cannot carry a URL, an '=' or whitespace - a credential-shaped 'KEY=VALUE' string has nowhere to go.

class_token.description: A classifier drawn from a small controlled vocabulary - 'replay-bundle', 'evidence.compacted'. Lower-case, punctuation-limited and short, because a classifier that can hold a sentence can hold a prompt, and one that can hold 2KB can hold a credential. Two bounds are load-bearing rather than tidy. maxLength is 40: a 256-bit key is 64 characters as hex and 44 as base64, so neither shape fits, and a review found a 64-character hex private key accepted as an object_class. The 'not' clause refuses a token that is nothing but hex from sixteen characters up, which closes the shorter hex forms that would still fit; below that a pure-hex token is a plausible classifier and too small to be key material. The lower-case pattern already excludes base64 and upper-case base32. A classifier this field cannot express is a sign the vocabulary needs a considered entry, not a longer field.

evidence_ref.description: A pointer into the existing verifier/evidence path, not a note about one and not a way to fetch one. Either a scheme-qualified reference or a repository-relative path whose final segment carries a file extension, so that the placeholders which satisfy a mere minLength - '   ', 'n/a', 'TODO' - do not satisfy an evidence requirement. The character set is the control. It previously admitted 222 characters including ? # & = % @, which is not the shape of a pointer - it is the shape of a presigned URL ('?X-Amz-Credential=...&X-Amz-Signature=...'), a token callback ('?token=...') and a basic-auth URL ('//user:pass@host'), all of which a review got accepted here. Query strings, fragments and userinfo are gone, because an evidence reference that carries its own authorisation is a credential stored in a manifest.

free_status_evidence.description: Where the free-status claim came from. The whole registry turns on this field: 'provider_documentation' is a marketing page and buys nothing, 'runtime_account_evidence' is something observed about this account and is the only class that can unlock a VERIFIED_* status.

authority_flags.description: Denied by name rather than by omission, matching storage_object_manifest.schema.json.
